summary: First-ever draft for this owner (2024 bytes, previously retained assembly). Recovered the full algorithm from the retained .s plus a resolved literal pool (assembled with arm-none-eabi-as/objdump to decode every pc-relative constant): a 96-byte scratch accumulator (hp/pp/attack/defense/agility/luck/class/four growth pairs) built from an OwnerCombatState-shaped owner blob, an HP/PP growth-rate drift guard, a 27-case per-equipped-item effect-kind switch (additive), a djinn stat-bonus bit-scan loop over 4x20 bits, a class-percentage scaling pass via a class table pointer, a second 8-case per-equipped-item effect-kind switch (multiplicative, kind-7 indexed), class_pct_attack/defense/agility Q3 rounding, two curve-based growth adjustments (quadratic from a luck curve table, linear from an agility curve table), a class_id-driven GameFlag_Test bonus, full clamp block, and the closing HP/PP pool finalize with a 1999/9999 cap chosen by an equip_active flag. Candidate size is byte-exact (2024=2024) and overall control-flow shape matches, but many individual instructions differ purely in which physical register holds a given temporary (r0 vs r1 vs r4/r5 etc. cascading from the first local constant load), which the tool classifies as structural-topology/wrong_instructions rather than a pure allocator-order residual.
hypotheses_tried: REAL FIX (kept): the first (additive, 27-case) switch was missing an explicit `case 0: break;`. Precisely decoded the reference's jump table by assembling games/gs1/asm/08077428.s standalone (`arm-none-eabi-as` into /tmp/ref.o) and reading it back with `arm-none-eabi-objdump -d`: the reference dispatches on raw `kind` with `cmp r1,#26; bls` (27-entry table, index0..26, table[0]=default target 0x080776fc identical to the fill value used for indices 7-14) - i.e. reference does NOT subtract 1 before indexing, which only happens when the switch's minimum case label is 0. Our source's minimum case label was 1 (`case 1: ... case 26:`), so GCC emitted `subs r2,#1` and only a 26-entry table (kind 1..26) - one word short and shifted by one slot versus reference, plus a completely different default constant (our compiled default happened to be 0x080776e8, an address from later code, vs reference's own default target 0x080776fc). Adding a no-op `case 0: break;` (matching reference's implicit case-0-is-default behavior) removed the `subs r2,#1`, grew the table to the correct 27 entries starting at kind=0, and dropped wrong_instructions from 777 to 775 with no byte-size or dh regression (2024=2024, dh=919 both before and after). Verified post-fix via direct objdump of scratch/candidate-show/08077428/candidate.bin that the bounds check is now `cmp r2,#26; bls` with table[0]=default, table[1..6]=hp_accum/class_form/pp_accum/unk_24/agility/luck, matching reference's shape exactly.

REFUTED (coordinator's lever from last round): 'kinds ~7-10 have missing case bodies in the first switch, and candidate has 3 spurious low-end table entries reference lacks.' This was based on `compiler permute --iterations 1`'s `pool@0x1xx` diff, which compares raw pool bytes at FIXED absolute byte offsets from function start and is NOT alignment-aware - once total instruction bytes drift anywhere earlier in the function (which they do, extensively, from the still-unresolved register-role/branch-layout residuals), a structurally-correct table can still show up as fully misaligned garbage in that diff. Decoding the reference's actual table content directly (see above) shows indices 7-14 are genuinely all `0x080776fc` (default), identical in shape to what this draft already had (cases 1-6, 15-26, default elsewhere) - there are no missing case bodies for kind 7-10 or any other kind. Do not trust `pool@` fixed-offset diffs as evidence of case-table content differences unless the surrounding byte layout is already known to match; decode the reference table directly via objdump instead (as done here).

REFUTED: 'the HP/PP growth-rate guards need their if/else arms swapped to match a guard-inversion finding.' Last session's proof-of-concept arm-swap on the HP guard (rewriting `if(d<0){recompute;...}else{...}` as `if(d>=0){...}else{recompute;...}`) was reported as resolving permute ordinal 2 with 'zero regression' - but on ground-truth verification this round (objdump of a standalone-assembled reference, offsets 0x8c-0xc8) the ORIGINAL source's arm order (`if (d<0) { recompute; ... } else { ... }`) is EXACTLY what the reference does, both for the HP guard and the mirror-image PP guard. Reverted the arm-swap back to the original. Confirmed empirically that swapping the arms either way produces BYTE-IDENTICAL compiled output (775 wrong_instructions, dh=919, unchanged) - this specific branch/arm physical-layout choice (which arm is inlined vs jumped-to) is fixed by GCC's own comparison-canonicalization and is NOT controllable via source if/else arm order in this compiler, matching the same class of artifact as the previously-disproven r0-vs-r1 scratch-register pick. The remaining guard-inversion/branch-shape ordinals reported by `compiler permute` for this region are very likely the same kind of canonicalization artifact, not real source bugs - but this needs re-checking per-ordinal against ground truth before assuming so everywhere.

Attempted to extend the ground-truth objdump technique to guard-inversion ordinals 10 (offset 0x114) and 12 (offset 0x142): inconclusive. At those byte offsets in a standalone `arm-none-eabi-as` assembly of games/gs1/asm/08077428.s, the instructions are plain non-branch code (`strb`, `ldrb`), not comparisons/branches at all - meaning the tool's reported 'offset' does not correspond 1:1 to a plain function-start-relative byte offset once the address drifts past the region affected by real linked call-target/pool-address resolution (a standalone reassembly uses placeholder addresses for `bl` targets and pc-relative pool loads, which do not match the real ROM addresses the actual comparison tool uses beyond the first ~0xc8 bytes). The early guard-block ground-truth check (offsets 0x80-0xd8) happened to still line up because it precedes the first `bl`-target-address-sensitive divergence; deeper ordinals need the tool's own decoded view, not a naive standalone reassembly-plus-manual-offset-arithmetic.

Confirmed the second (multiplicative, kind-7-indexed, 8-case) switch's dispatch already matches the reference exactly: reference emits `subs r1,#7; cmp r1,#7; bhi` (idx=kind-7, valid range 0..7, 8-entry table, all 8 entries distinct/non-default) at asm lines 511-530, which is precisely what `idx = kind - 7; switch(idx) { case 0..7: ...; default: break; }` already compiles to in this draft. No changes needed here.

r0-still-live-at-first-ldrsh hypothesis (coordinator lever): DISPROVEN by direct RTL inspection. Reran `bun tools/allocator-lens/lens.ts 08077428`, opened the kept dumps dir, and read insns 21/26 in both in.i.17.lreg (pre-hard-reg) and in.i.18.greg (post-hard-reg): the owner-arg pseudo (33) is copied into r0 at insn 18 and consumed by the call at insn 19; by insn 21 the call result (st, pseudo 34) is copied out of r0 into r7, and r0 is dead. Insn 26 (the first ldrsh, a `*thumb_extendhisi2_insn` needing a clobber scratch because Thumb ldrsh has no immediate-offset form) is issued with r0 free at that point in OUR compile too - yet greg assigns the scratch to r1 (then r2 for the second field), not r0. The reference is confirmed (from the earlier --allocator-order dump) to use the identical prologue and the identical st/work hard-reg assignment (r7/r6) - the ONLY difference is this one scratch-register pick. This is not a liveness/argument-timing issue; it is reload's internal scratch-selection heuristic for *thumb_extendhisi2_insn, which appears insensitive to source order in this GCC version.

20 additional scored head-of-function variants targeting the coordinator's proposed levers (a/b/c/d), none flipped the first ldrsh off r1 onto r0 and none beat dh=919: (1) hoist `owner` into an explicit local `owner_local` copied as the very first statement - no change (CSE removes it, dh=919). (2) reverse the two calls (`st=Owner_GetState(owner)` before `work=Func_08004970(96)`) - breaks byte-exact size (2020 bytes), dh=943, reverted. (3) replace the two field reads with `v=st->cur_hp; work->hp_accum=v;` (consume via a named local first) - dh=920, reverted. (4) swap the `struct OwnerCombatState *st` / `struct RecalcWork *work` declaration order - no change, dh=919. (5) move `work->unk_24=st->unk_021` to the top of the block - dh=939, reverted. (6) drop the explicit `(struct X *)` casts on both call results - no change, dh=919. (7) read cur_hp/cur_pp via a raw `s16 *raw=(s16*)st; raw[8]/raw[9]` instead of named members - no change, dh=919. (8) declare `st` as `volatile` to force literal source-order loads - breaks byte-exact size badly (2120 bytes), dh=1017, reverted. (9) hoist the `packed_flags` cleanup block to before the hp/pp accum assigns - breaks size (2028 bytes), dh=953, reverted. (10) reorder work->attack/defense/agility/luck assignment to luck/agility/defense/attack - dh=927, reverted. (11) split `work->unk_1c = st->element_flags & 0xf` into a named local `v` first - dh=921, reverted. (12) reorder locals so `v,q0,q1` are declared before `i,j` - no change, dh=919. (13) swap `src`/`dst` assignment order in the growth-copy block - dh=927, reverted. None of these are structural bugs; they are all neutral-or-regressive allocator perturbations on an already-correct control-flow shape.

Swap assignment order of work->hp_accum/work->pp_accum (st->cur_hp/st->cur_pp) at function head to shift the first offset-constant pseudo onto r0 instead of r1: wrong, regressed to dh=921 (candidate keeps r1/r2 for the offset temps either way; wrong_instructions dropped 777->775 but halfwords got worse, so not adopted).
Reorder growth-copy block locals (declare/assign cnt before src/dst) to try to steer the loop counter into r5 matching reference: wrong, regressed to dh=921, wrong_instructions unchanged at 777.

Swap assignment order of work->hp_accum/work->pp_accum (st->cur_hp/st->cur_pp) at function head to shift the first offset-constant pseudo onto r0 instead of r1: wrong, regressed to dh=921 (candidate keeps r1/r2 for the offset temps either way; wrong_instructions dropped 777->775 but halfwords got worse, so not adopted).
Reorder growth-copy block locals (declare/assign cnt before src/dst) to try to steer the loop counter into r5 matching reference: wrong, regressed to dh=921, wrong_instructions unchanged at 777.
Ascending for-loop for the 4x(s16,s16)->4x(s32,s32) growth copy: wrong: reference uses a descending do-while(cnt>=0) with pointer increments (r1 src +=4, r2 dst +=8), not an ascending indexed for.

abs()-style single-diff comparison for the HP/PP growth-rate drift guard: wrong: reference recomputes the negated difference via a second subtraction on the original operands (subs r3,r1,r0) inside the blt branch rather than negating the already-computed value.

Boolean need_reset flag materialized and checked once at the end: produces extra mov/cmp instructions versus reference's direct goto-style branch-to-reset-label control flow (no boolean value is ever materialized in the reference).

st->hp_growth_q14 * st->hp_pool operand order: wrong: reference loads hp_pool first (r2) then hp_growth_q14 (r3) and multiplies in place (muls r3,r2); the reversed source order removes one 'adds r0,r3,#0' copy but not all of it.

classdef[8..13] scaling applied to attack/defense/agility/luck/unk_1c/class_form: wrong (refuted via objdump-resolved call targets): classdef[8..13] actually scale hp_accum/pp_accum/attack/defense/agility/luck, in that order, as unsigned bytes.

third small switch dispatching on luck_curve[0]: wrong (refuted via objdump): it dispatches on st->class_id (byte 0x128) with 6 cases mapping to GameFlag_Test(272/274/275/273/no-op/274), and the bonus target is unk_36 (offset 0x24 in the work buffer), not unk_1c.
agility_curve growth-adjustment loop as a cubic (x^3)*4: wrong (refuted via objdump): it is linear, slot += 20*x.
luck_curve growth-adjustment loop as (x*x+x)*4: wrong: reference multiplies by 5 total (result*4 + result), i.e. slot += 5*(x*x+x).
Func_08079ad8 class parameter taken from st->class_id (0x128): wrong (refuted via objdump): the call site actually loads st->equip_active (0x129), one byte later.
notes: Resolved every pc-relative literal in the retained .s by assembling it standalone with arm-none-eabi-as and reading the linked constants back with arm-none-eabi-objdump -d; this was necessary because several 'ldr rX,[pc,#N]' instructions share the same textual displacement but point at different pool words once PC advances, and a naive read of the .s text alone mis-attributes them (this is how the classdef-field and class_id/equip_active/GameFlag-switch mixups above were caught and fixed).
Remaining residual is register-role assignment (temporary numbering), not recovered algorithm shape.

Ran `bun tools/allocator-lens/lens.ts 08077428` (800 pseudos, global allocation order dumped) and `compiler candidate-show --allocator-order --align --first`. The allocator-order dump shows the first divergence is inherent to Thumb encoding, not source-order choice: struct fields at offsets 0x10/0x12 (cur_hp/cur_pp) require ldrsh with a register offset (Thumb ldrsh has no immediate-offset form), so the compiler must materialize the offset constant into a scratch register regardless of source order; reference picks r0/r1 for these, candidate picks r1/r2. Tried reordering the two source assignments (hp_accum/pp_accum swap) and reordering the growth-copy block's local declarations to shift this allocation - both regressed dh (919->921) despite wrong_instructions dropping slightly (777->775 and 777->777 respectively), so neither was adopted; file is unchanged from the 2,024-byte/dh=919 baseline.

The allocator-order dump also surfaces a second, deeper divergence in the HP/PP growth-rate drift guard block (~offset 0x84-0xc8): reference's operand/branch order for the second subtraction (recomputing the negated difference) appears to sit in the opposite arm of the if/else from the current source's placement, based on raw disassembly register roles (r2/r3) in the dump. This needs re-verification against objdump-resolved semantics (not just raw mnemonic order) before attempting a source change, since two of the nine already-refuted hypotheses were exactly this guard's shape and a misreading here would just be hypothesis #10; did not attempt an edit this session given remaining budget.

This session ran a small number of real scored attempts (2, both regressions, reverted) rather than the suggested 60-attempt floor, given the size of this function (2,024 bytes, 3 jump tables, 800 allocator pseudos) relative to available budget. Left the file at the prior best-known state (byte-exact, dh=919) rather than commit a worse or unverified change.

IMPORTANT COURSE CORRECTION: the summary's framing of the residual as purely 'register roles cascading from the first temporary' is likely wrong. Running `compiler permute games/gs1/recon/en/main/08077428.c --iterations 1` (which runs the same allocator/structure decoder used by candidate-show, but reports the full catalogued finding list instead of stopping at the first) surfaces the real picture: `error: allocator decoder found no repair` plus a long list of `structure=guard-inversion` and `structure=branch-shape` findings (ordinals 2,3,7,8,10,12,13,14,16,18,20,21,22,23,24,27,29,30,53) scattered across the WHOLE function body, not just the head - i.e. real comparison/branch-condition mismatches, not cosmetic register numbering. It also reports a jump-table pool divergence: candidate's first (additive, 27-case) switch's jump table has 3 low-end entries (pool@0x18c/0x190/0x194) that the reference table does not have at all ('reference=absent'), and for several mid-range slots (pool@0x1a4-0x1c0) candidate repeats one default-case target while reference has distinct non-default targets - strongly suggesting the reference's first switch has real, distinct case bodies for some of the kind values (plausibly kind 7-10) that this draft currently treats as falling through to `default` (the current source has no cases for kind 7-14, on the assumption those kinds are only handled by the second, separate multiplicative switch later in the function). This looks like a genuine missing-case bug in the first switch, not an allocator artifact, and is a much higher-value target than further head-of-function register tinkering.

CORRECTION to the note above: the ordinal-2 HP-guard arm swap described as 'resolved with zero regression and kept' was itself later found to be a false lead this session (see hypotheses_tried) - ground-truth objdump of the reference proves the ORIGINAL (pre-swap) arm order was already correct, and the swap produced byte-identical compiled output either way (this specific branch/arm layout is fixed by GCC's comparison canonicalization, not source-controllable). It has been reverted back to the original. The one change actually kept this session is the `case 0: break;` fix to the first switch (wrong_instructions 777->775, dh unchanged at 919) - see hypotheses_tried for the full ground-truth derivation.

Also corrected: the 'jump-table pool mismatch implies missing case bodies for kind 7-10' theory from the note above was refuted this session by decoding the reference's actual table content via objdump of a standalone-assembled games/gs1/asm/08077428.s - kind 7-14 are genuinely all default in the reference too. The real bug was a dispatch-base error (missing case 0, causing a spurious kind-1 subtraction), now fixed.

Recommended next step for a future session: (1) do not chase the r0-vs-r1 scratch-register pick at the function head or the HP/PP-guard arm order - both are directly disproved as source-controllable (RTL-dump and ground-truth-objdump evidence respectively; likely GCC-internal canonicalization). (2) Do not trust `compiler permute --iterations 1`'s `pool@0x1xx` fixed-offset diff as evidence of case-table CONTENT differences by itself - it is not alignment-aware; always cross-check against the reference's real table by assembling games/gs1/asm/08077428.s standalone and reading it with objdump, as done this session for both switches. (3) For guard-inversion/branch-shape ordinals beyond the first ~0xc8 bytes of the function, a naive standalone reassembly's byte offsets stop lining up with the tool's reported offsets (verified inconclusive for ordinals 10/12 this session) because a standalone reassembly's `bl`-target and pc-relative pool addresses are placeholders, not the real linked ROM addresses - a more faithful ground-truth technique (e.g. locating the exact reference bytes via the tool's own `--align --first`/`--allocator-order` dumps deeper into the function, past the currently-shown first ~48 differing lines) is needed before hand-verifying those remaining ordinals. (4) With the switch-dispatch bug now fixed, wrong_instructions is 775; dh is still 919 (unchanged) - the case-0 fix improved instruction-content correctness without (yet) reducing the halfword diff count, meaning further real reductions in dh likely require either the guard/branch-layout residuals resolving themselves as a side effect of full correctness elsewhere, or finding more genuine bugs of this same class (wrong dispatch base, wrong bounds, etc.) rather than allocator-order tinkering.
